info.name: API Platform Demo - Gateway Management
info.description:
Deploys this project's gateway artifacts directly against the gateway-controller's management REST API (port 9090, basic auth) -- separate from the main "API Platform Demo" collection, which invokes the APIs' business endpoints on the data plane.

Every request's raw body is the verbatim contents of a YAML file in this repo, so editing a body in Postman is a throwaway experiment -- to keep a change, edit the file and re-import.

**Source of truth.** The two demo APIs' gateway definitions live at the repo root and nowhere else:
  - AgentChatAPI-v1.0      agent-chat-rate-limiting/AgentChatAPI-v1.0.yaml
  - OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 order-management-dynamic-routing/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml

The AgentChatAPI and OrderManagementAPI bodies below (1c, 2a, 3c, 3f) are copied verbatim from those two files. The per-org copies under artifacts/via-script/<org>/apis/ are gone -- do not re-add them.

**Folder 1 - Seed the public catalog (prerequisite).** The five artifacts the README lists as "already deployed to the gateway" before the demo starts, read from artifacts/via-script/public/:
  - REST  WeatherAPI-v1.0        apis/weather-api-v1.0/WeatherAPI-v1.0.yaml
  - REST  AirQualityAPI-v1.0     apis/air-quality-api-v1.0/AirQualityAPI-v1.0.yaml
  - REST  AgentChatAPI-v1.0      ../agent-chat-rate-limiting/AgentChatAPI-v1.0.yaml  (repo root, not via-script)
  - MCP   geo-mcp-server-v1.0     mcps/geo-mcp-server-v1.0/geo-mcp-server-v1.0.yaml
  - MCP   weather-mcp-server-v1.0 mcps/weather-mcp-server-v1.0/weather-mcp-server-v1.0.yaml

This is the Postman equivalent of `./scripts/seed-gateway.sh`, which deploys the same five artifacts (it routes each file by its own `kind:` -- RestApi to /rest-apis, Mcp to /mcp-proxies).

**Folder 2 - Deploy OrderManagementAPI (README step 1).** The "add a new API live" step: creates OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 from order-management-dynamic-routing/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml. Publish it into the Developer Portal afterwards with folder 2 of the main "API Platform Demo" collection.

**Folder 4 - Protocol-bridging demos.** The SOAP and OData demo APIs, each with create, update and undeploy:
  - REST  LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0  legacy-order-service/LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0.yaml  (SOAP backend behind a REST API)
  - REST  ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0      product-catalog-odata/ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0.yaml     (OData v4 backend, no policies needed)
Both need their mock backend running (ports 7196 and 7194).

**Folder 3 - Update (idempotent re-push).** A PUT for every artifact above. Folders 1 and 2 only work the FIRST time -- rerunning a create returns 409 Conflict. Folder 3 is safe to rerun any time.

REST APIs go to /api/management/v1/rest-apis, MCP proxies to /api/management/v1/mcp-proxies.

Set `gateway_mgmt_url` to the gateway's MANAGEMENT listener -- not the port APIs are invoked on. The deployed EC2 setup uses http://platform.gw.wso2.com:9090.

# AgentChatAPI-v1.0 — per-org AND per-org-per-use-case token budgets for
# calls to the WK AI agent, each an explicit, independently-configurable
# quota (not a single generic auto-bucketed quota) via advanced-ratelimit's
# match-gated keyExtraction. Renamed from TokenBasedThrottlingAPI-v1.0 to
# reflect a real business scenario: rate-limiting chat/completion calls to
# an LLM-style agent backend by customer org and by use-case, based on
# actual token usage (not just request count).
#
# PROTECTED: jwt-auth verifies the caller's token against either of two
# WSO2 IS key managers (IS-railco, IS-acme -- see
# [policy_configurations.jwtauth_v1] in config.toml). Org identity for
# rate-limit bucketing comes from the X-Org-Name request header (type:
# header), NOT the verified JWT claim -- jwt-auth is used here purely to
# authenticate the caller, not to establish org identity. Use-case
# identity is likewise a plain header (X-Use-Case-Id).
#
# Each org has its own org-wide budget PLUS its own per-use-case budgets, all
# checked independently — any one being exhausted blocks the call even if
# the others still have room. Limit values below are demo placeholders; swap
# in the real per-customer numbers when available.
#
# Deploy (create — first time):
#   curl -X POST "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @configs/AgentChatAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Update (subsequent changes):
#   curl -X PUT "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis/AgentChatAPI-v1.0" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @configs/AgentChatAPI-v1.0.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: RestApi
metadata:
  name: AgentChatAPI-v1.0
spec:
  displayName: AgentChatAPI
  version: v1.0
  context: /agent/$version
  upstream:
    main:
      url: http://host.docker.internal:7094   # mock-backends/mock-agent-backend.js
  policies:
    - name: jwt-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers: ["IS-railco", "IS-acme"]
    - name: advanced-ratelimit
      version: v1
      params:
        quotas:
          # ---- Railco ----
          - name: railco-org-token-budget
            limits:
              - limit: 500
                duration: "1m"
            keyExtraction:
              - type: header
                key: X-Org-Name
                match: { type: regex, value: "^railco$" }
            costExtraction:
              enabled: true
              sources:
                - type: response_header
                  key: X-Completion-Tokens
              default: 10

          - name: railco-usecase1-token-budget
            limits:
              - limit: 200
                duration: "1m"
            keyExtraction:
              - type: header
                key: X-Org-Name
                match: { type: regex, value: "^railco$" }
              - type: header
                key: X-Use-Case-Id
                match: { type: regex, value: "^usecase1$" }
            costExtraction:
              enabled: true
              sources:
                - type: response_header
                  key: X-Completion-Tokens
              default: 10

          - name: railco-usecase2-token-budget
            limits:
              - limit: 100
                duration: "1m"
            keyExtraction:
              - type: header
                key: X-Org-Name
                match: { type: regex, value: "^railco$" }
              - type: header
                key: X-Use-Case-Id
                match: { type: regex, value: "^usecase2$" }
            costExtraction:
              enabled: true
              sources:
                - type: response_header
                  key: X-Completion-Tokens
              default: 10

          # ---- Acme ----
          - name: acme-org-token-budget
            limits:
              - limit: 150
                duration: "1m"
            keyExtraction:
              - type: header
                key: X-Org-Name
                match: { type: regex, value: "^acme$" }
            costExtraction:
              enabled: true
              sources:
                - type: response_header
                  key: X-Completion-Tokens
              default: 10

          - name: acme-usecase1-token-budget
            limits:
              - limit: 50
                duration: "1m"
            keyExtraction:
              - type: header
                key: X-Org-Name
                match: { type: regex, value: "^acme$" }
              - type: header
                key: X-Use-Case-Id
                match: { type: regex, value: "^usecase1$" }
            costExtraction:
              enabled: true
              sources:
                - type: response_header
                  key: X-Completion-Tokens
              default: 10

          - name: acme-usecase2-token-budget
            limits:
              - limit: 70
                duration: "1m"
            keyExtraction:
              - type: header
                key: X-Org-Name
                match: { type: regex, value: "^acme$" }
              - type: header
                key: X-Use-Case-Id
                match: { type: regex, value: "^usecase2$" }
            costExtraction:
              enabled: true
              sources:
                - type: response_header
                  key: X-Completion-Tokens
              default: 10
  operations:
    - method: POST
      path: /chat/completions

# geo-mcp-server-v1.0 — gateway-deployable MCP proxy for the Geo MCP Server
# bundle. This is the GATEWAY half of the bundle (runtime route + tool
# surface); api-portal/ alongside it is the PORTAL half (catalog metadata +
# the tool list the portal renders). Neither reads the other.
#
# The tool set here mirrors api-portal/definition.yaml, re-expressed in the
# gateway's own shape: MCPTool.inputSchema is a STRING holding a JSON Schema
# document (see MCPTool in gateway-controller/api/management-openapi.yaml),
# not a nested YAML mapping as in the portal definition.
#
# DUMMY UPSTREAM: no real MCP server ships with this bundle, so upstream.url
# below points at a placeholder port that nothing listens on. The proxy
# deploys and lists its tools, but an actual tools/call will fail to connect
# until a real MCP server is put behind it. Swap upstream.url for the real
# server's address when there is one.
#
# Deploy (create — first time):
#   curl -X POST "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/mcp-proxies" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: text/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @geo-mcp-server-v1.0.yaml
#
# Update (subsequent changes):
#   curl -X PUT "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/mcp-proxies/geo-mcp-server-v1.0" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: text/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @geo-mcp-server-v1.0.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: geo-mcp-server-v1.0
spec:
  displayName: Geo MCP Server
  version: v1.0
  context: /mcp/geo
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://host.docker.internal:7101   # dummy — no real geo MCP server ships with this bundle
  tools:
    - name: geocodeAddress
      title: Geocode Address
      description: Resolve a free-text place name or address into coordinates.
      inputSchema: |
        {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "query": {
              "type": "string",
              "description": "Place name or address to resolve, e.g. \"Colombo, Sri Lanka\""
            }
          },
          "required": ["query"]
        }
    - name: reverseGeocode
      title: Reverse Geocode
      description: Resolve a lat/lon pair into a human-readable place name.
      inputSchema: |
        {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "lat": {
              "type": "number",
              "description": "Latitude"
            },
            "lon": {
              "type": "number",
              "description": "Longitude"
            }
          },
          "required": ["lat", "lon"]
        }

      title: Get Forecast

              "minimum": 1,
              "maximum": 10
            }
          },
          "required": ["location"]

item.name: 2. Deploy OrderManagementAPI
item.description: Deploys order-management-dynamic-routing/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml -- the REST API added live during the demo (README step 1). After this, the API Publisher discovers it; publish it to the Developer Portal with the main collection's portal folder.

body.raw:
# OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 — routes each customer's order request to their
# own tenant-specific Order Management backend, and exchanges the caller's
# own token for a backend-specific token via the tenant's token-exchange
# service before dispatch. Uses the custom `dynamic-routing` policy
# (policies/dynamic-routing), already compiled into this gateway's image —
# see docs/dynamic-routing-custom-policy.md for the policy's own design
# notes. Renamed from DynamicRoutingAPI-v1.0 to reflect a real business
# scenario: Railco and Acme are customer tenants, each with their own OMS.
#
# No orgUpstreamMap param below: org_id's raw value IS the
# upstreamDefinitions entry name directly (see the entries named "Railco"
# and "Acme" below) — a caller whose org_id claim is "Railco" routes
# straight to the "Railco" upstreamDefinitions entry, no separate map.
# Deliberate tradeoff: an org_id with no matching upstreamDefinitions entry
# (e.g. a typo) gets a 502/503 from the kernel rather than falling back to
# the default upstream below — the SDK gives this policy no way to verify a
# candidate name against upstreamDefinitions to do that safely.
#
# PROTECTED: jwt-auth verifies the caller's token against either of two
# WSO2 IS key managers (IS-railco, IS-acme -- see
# [policy_configurations.jwtauth_v1] in config.toml), authenticating the
# caller only. dynamic-routing reads org_id from the X-Org-Name request
# header instead -- not any token claim. Requests without a valid token are
# rejected by jwt-auth; requests with a valid token but no X-Org-Name header
# are rejected by dynamic-routing itself (503).
#
# Deploy (create — first time):
#   curl -X POST "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @configs/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Update (subsequent changes):
#   curl -X PUT "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @configs/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Requires (all already running from earlier work):
#   - mock-services/wk-token-exchange-service.js   (PORT=7099)
#   - mock-backends/mock-backend.js NAME=railco_backend PORT=7093
#   - mock-backends/mock-backend.js NAME=acme_backend   PORT=7095
#   - mock-backends/mock-backend.js NAME=default_backend PORT=7096
#   - WSO2 IS instance on :9444 (IS-railco and IS-acme key managers) -- a
#     real, currently-valid access token is still required (jwt-auth rejects
#     dummy bearer tokens); the X-Org-Name header determines routing.
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: RestApi
metadata:
  name: OrderManagementAPI-v1.0
spec:
  displayName: OrderManagementAPI
  version: v1.0
  context: /order-management/$version
  upstream:
    main:
      url: http://host.docker.internal:7096   # default/fallback — used when org_id has no matching upstreamDefinitions entry
  upstreamDefinitions:
    - name: railco
      upstreams:
        - url: http://host.docker.internal:7093
    - name: acme
      upstreams:
        - url: http://host.docker.internal:7095
  policies:
    - name: jwt-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers: ["IS-railco","IS-acme"]
    - name: dynamic-routing
      version: v1
      params:
        # Name of the request header carrying the caller's org id.
        # Config-only change, no rebuild needed.
        orgIDHeader: "X-Org-Name"
        exchangeServiceUrl: "http://host.docker.internal:7099/exchange"
        # Header the exchanged backend-specific token is sent to the backend
        # in, as "Bearer <token>". The caller's original Authorization header
        # is dropped before forwarding -- the backend only ever sees this
        # header, never the caller's own token. Config-only change, no
        # rebuild needed.
        backendTokenHeader: "Backend-Token"
  operations:
    - method: POST
      path: /orders

Creates OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 on the gateway-controller's management API, from order-management-dynamic-routing/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml.

# OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 — routes each customer's order request to their
# own tenant-specific Order Management backend, and exchanges the caller's
# own token for a backend-specific token via the tenant's token-exchange
# service before dispatch. Uses the custom `dynamic-routing` policy
# (policies/dynamic-routing), already compiled into this gateway's image —
# see docs/dynamic-routing-custom-policy.md for the policy's own design
# notes. Renamed from DynamicRoutingAPI-v1.0 to reflect a real business
# scenario: Railco and Acme are customer tenants, each with their own OMS.
#
# No orgUpstreamMap param below: org_id's raw value IS the
# upstreamDefinitions entry name directly (see the entries named "Railco"
# and "Acme" below) — a caller whose org_id claim is "Railco" routes
# straight to the "Railco" upstreamDefinitions entry, no separate map.
# Deliberate tradeoff: an org_id with no matching upstreamDefinitions entry
# (e.g. a typo) gets a 502/503 from the kernel rather than falling back to
# the default upstream below — the SDK gives this policy no way to verify a
# candidate name against upstreamDefinitions to do that safely.
#
# PROTECTED: jwt-auth verifies the caller's token against either of two
# WSO2 IS key managers (IS-railco, IS-acme -- see
# [policy_configurations.jwtauth_v1] in config.toml), authenticating the
# caller only. dynamic-routing reads org_id from the X-Org-Name request
# header instead -- not any token claim. Requests without a valid token are
# rejected by jwt-auth; requests with a valid token but no X-Org-Name header
# are rejected by dynamic-routing itself (503).
#
# Deploy (create — first time):
#   curl -X POST "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @configs/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Update (subsequent changes):
#   curl -X PUT "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0" \
#     -u "admin:admin" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @configs/OrderManagementAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Requires (all already running from earlier work):
#   - mock-services/wk-token-exchange-service.js   (PORT=7099)
#   - mock-backends/mock-backend.js NAME=railco_backend PORT=7093
#   - mock-backends/mock-backend.js NAME=acme_backend   PORT=7095
#   - mock-backends/mock-backend.js NAME=default_backend PORT=7096
#   - WSO2 IS instance on :9444 (IS-railco and IS-acme key managers) -- a
#     real, currently-valid access token is still required (jwt-auth rejects
#     dummy bearer tokens); the X-Org-Name header determines routing.
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: RestApi
metadata:
  name: OrderManagementAPI-v1.0
spec:
  displayName: OrderManagementAPI
  version: v1.0
  context: /order-management/$version
  upstream:
    main:
      url: http://host.docker.internal:7096   # default/fallback — used when org_id has no matching upstreamDefinitions entry
  upstreamDefinitions:
    - name: railco
      upstreams:
        - url: http://host.docker.internal:7093
    - name: acme
      upstreams:
        - url: http://host.docker.internal:7095
  policies:
    - name: jwt-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers: ["IS-railco","IS-acme"]
    - name: dynamic-routing
      version: v1
      params:
        # Name of the request header carrying the caller's org id.
        # Config-only change, no rebuild needed.
        orgIDHeader: "X-Org-Name"
        exchangeServiceUrl: "http://host.docker.internal:7099/exchange"
        # Header the exchanged backend-specific token is sent to the backend
        # in, as "Bearer <token>". The caller's original Authorization header
        # is dropped before forwarding -- the backend only ever sees this
        # header, never the caller's own token. Config-only change, no
        # rebuild needed.
        backendTokenHeader: "Backend-Token"
  operations:
    - method: POST
      path: /orders

item.name: 4. Protocol-bridging demos (deploy / update / undeploy)
item.description:
The two protocol-bridging demo APIs, each with its full lifecycle: create, idempotent update, and undeploy.

Unlike folders 1-3, undeploy (DELETE) requests live here beside their create requests rather than in a folder of their own -- these two APIs are demo-only and get torn down and re-deployed often.

Source of truth, as everywhere else in this collection -- the raw bodies below are copied verbatim from these files:
  - LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0  legacy-order-service/LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0.yaml
  - ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0      product-catalog-odata/ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0.yaml

Both APIs need their mock backend running on the machine the gateway resolves as host.docker.internal:
  - SOAP:  NAME=order_soap_backend PORT=7196 node mock-soap-backend.js
  - OData: SERVICE_ROOT=<gateway base url> NAME=catalog_odata_backend PORT=7194 node mock-odata-backend.js

SERVICE_ROOT matters: without it the OData service emits @odata.context and @odata.nextLink URLs pointing at the backend rather than the gateway.

body.raw:
# LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0 — exposes a legacy SOAP Order Management
# service as a plain JSON/REST API. Callers speak JSON; the gateway speaks
# SOAP/XML to the backend. Nothing else: no auth, no rate limiting, no
# dynamic routing -- this API exists purely to demonstrate SOAP-to-REST
# proxying via the json-xml-mediator policy.
#
# Three policies, each doing one job:
#
#   json-xml-mediator (v1.0.4)
#     The whole point of this API. downsteamPayloadFormat: json /
#     upstreamPayloadFormat: xml means the caller's JSON request body is
#     converted to XML on the way to the backend, and the backend's XML
#     response is converted back to JSON on the way out. (The parameter
#     really is spelled "downsteam" -- that typo is in the policy's own
#     schema, see /app/policies/json-xml-mediator-v1.0.4.yaml in the
#     gateway-controller image. Using the correct spelling fails
#     validation.)
#
#     Two things about the conversion, both verified against this gateway
#     rather than assumed:
#
#     1. The generated XML is always wrapped in a synthetic <root> element,
#        so the backend receives
#          <root><Envelope><Body><GetOrder>...</GetOrder></Body></Envelope></root>
#        This is NOT a strictly valid SOAP envelope -- Envelope has to be
#        the document root. mock-soap-backend.js dispatches on the first
#        child of <Body> (falling back to SOAPAction), so it accepts this;
#        a strict SOAP stack such as Axis2 or .NET WCF would not. For a
#        real legacy backend, put an interceptor-service or a custom
#        policy after this one to unwrap <root>.
#     2. The conversion is not namespace-aware. A JSON key containing a
#        colon does not become a namespace prefix -- "soap:Envelope"
#        becomes <soap_Envelope originalKey="soap:Envelope">, and "@xmlns"
#        keys become elements, not attributes. So the envelope below is
#        deliberately prefix-free and namespace-free.
#
#     The mediator requires the INCOMING Content-Type to be exactly
#     application/json, and it rewrites the upstream Content-Type to
#     application/xml itself. Do not set Content-Type with set-headers
#     below: set-headers runs first, and overwriting the caller's
#     application/json makes the mediator fail the request with
#     500 "Content-Type must be application/json for downstream payload
#     format json".
#
#   request-rewrite (v1.0.2)
#     Every REST path is rewritten to the backend's single SOAP endpoint,
#     /OrderService. Without this the backend would be called at /orders,
#     /orders/get etc.
#
#   set-headers (v1.1.0), per operation
#     Sets the SOAPAction header each SOAP operation expects. This is
#     attached per-operation, not API-wide, because the value differs per
#     operation -- it is what lets one REST path map to one SOAP
#     operation.
#
# Because the envelope structure comes from the caller's JSON (no policy
# here can synthesize it), each REST operation is a POST whose body mirrors
# the SOAP envelope. See api-portal/definition.yaml for the exact schemas.
#
# Deploy (create — first time):
#   curl -X POST "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis" \
#     -u "admin:<GW_ADMIN_PASSWORD>" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Update (subsequent changes):
#   curl -X PUT "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis/LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0" \
#     -u "admin:<GW_ADMIN_PASSWORD>" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Requires:
#   - mock-services/mock-soap-backend.js  NAME=order_soap_backend PORT=7196
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: RestApi
metadata:
  name: LegacyOrderServiceAPI-v1.0
spec:
  displayName: LegacyOrderServiceAPI
  version: v1.0
  context: /legacy-order-service/$version
  upstream:
    main:
      url: http://host.docker.internal:7196   # mock-services/mock-soap-backend.js
  policies:
    # Policy versions are major-only here (v1). The gateway rejects a full
    # semantic version: "policy version must be major-only (e.g., v1)".
    - name: json-xml-mediator
      version: v1
      params:
        downsteamPayloadFormat: json   # what the REST caller sends/receives
        upstreamPayloadFormat: xml     # what the SOAP backend sends/receives
    - name: request-rewrite
      version: v1
      params:
        pathRewrite:
          type: ReplaceFullPath
          replaceFullPath: /OrderService
  operations:
    - method: POST
      path: /orders
      policies:
        - name: set-headers
          version: v1
          params:
            request:
              headers:
                - name: SOAPAction
                  value: "http://wso2.com/demo/order-management/CreateOrder"
    - method: POST
      path: /orders/get
      policies:
        - name: set-headers
          version: v1
          params:
            request:
              headers:
                - name: SOAPAction
                  value: "http://wso2.com/demo/order-management/GetOrder"
    - method: POST
      path: /orders/list
      policies:
        - name: set-headers
          version: v1
          params:
            request:
              headers:
                - name: SOAPAction
                  value: "http://wso2.com/demo/order-management/ListOrders"

# ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0 — exposes an OData v4 Product Catalog service as a
# REST API on the gateway. Deliberately minimal: no auth, no rate limiting,
# no dynamic routing.
#
# Unlike the SOAP demo next door (../legacy-order-service), this one needs
# NO mediation policy at all. OData v4 is already REST over HTTP with JSON
# payloads, so there is nothing to transcode -- the gateway's job here is
# routing, and later whatever auth and quotas you choose to bolt on.
#
# THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS: the catch-all path.
#
#   OData URLs are open-ended. A client may ask for /Products,
#   /Products(3), /Products(3)/Name, /Products(3)/Supplier, /$metadata, or
#   the service document at /. You cannot enumerate them as operations.
#
#   Verified against this gateway (1.2.1):
#     path: /*         -> TRUE multi-segment catch-all. Matches
#                         /Products(3)/Supplier. This is what OData needs.
#     path: /{path}    -> single segment ONLY. /Products(3) matches but
#                         /Products(3)/Name returns 404. Not enough.
#     path: /Products({id})
#                      -> works and is templated, but you would have to
#                         enumerate every shape. Use it only if you want to
#                         deliberately restrict the surface (see below).
#
#   So each HTTP method is declared once against /*.
#
# Query options ($filter, $select, $expand, $top, $skip, $orderby, $count)
# need no configuration whatsoever -- they are ordinary query strings and
# pass through untouched.
#
# SECURITY NOTE ON /*: a catch-all exposes the WHOLE OData service,
# including $metadata (which publishes your entity model) and every entity
# set the backend serves. That is usually what you want for an OData proxy
# and is why it is the default here. To restrict it instead, replace the
# /* operations with explicit ones -- e.g. only
#   - { method: GET, path: /Products }
#   - { method: GET, path: /Products({id}) }
# -- and the rest of the service stops being reachable through the gateway.
#
# THE URL-LEAK PROBLEM, and why it is fixed in the backend and not here:
#
#   OData responses embed ABSOLUTE URLs -- @odata.context, @odata.nextLink,
#   Location on create. By default they name the BACKEND, so a client that
#   follows @odata.nextLink to page through results would leave the gateway
#   entirely, or fail if the backend is not reachable from its network.
#
#   No stock policy rewrites a response BODY. host-rewrite only sets the
#   upstream Host request header, which is a different thing. The fix is to
#   tell the OData service its own public root, which every real OData
#   stack supports (SAP Gateway, Apache Olingo, WCF Data Services) and the
#   mock here takes as SERVICE_ROOT:
#
#     SERVICE_ROOT=http://localhost:8080/product-catalog/v1.0 \
#     NAME=catalog_odata_backend PORT=7194 node mock-odata-backend.js
#
#   If a backend genuinely cannot be told its public root, the only
#   remaining option is an interceptor-service on the response phase
#   (includeResponseBody: true) rewriting the URLs -- a network hop on
#   every response and a service you have to run. Prefer SERVICE_ROOT.
#
# Deploy (create — first time):
#   curl -X POST "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis" \
#     -u "admin:<GW_ADMIN_PASSWORD>" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Update (subsequent changes):
#   curl -X PUT "http://localhost:9090/api/management/v1/rest-apis/ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0" \
#     -u "admin:<GW_ADMIN_PASSWORD>" -H "Content-Type: application/yaml" \
#     --data-binary @ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0.yaml
#
# Requires:
#   - mock-services/mock-odata-backend.js  NAME=catalog_odata_backend PORT=7194
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: RestApi
metadata:
  name: ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0
spec:
  displayName: ProductCatalogAPI
  version: v1.0
  context: /product-catalog/$version
  upstream:
    main:
      url: http://host.docker.internal:7194   # mock-services/mock-odata-backend.js
  # No policies. OData v4 is already JSON/REST; nothing needs mediating.
  operations:
    # GET covers the service document, $metadata, collections, entities by
    # key, property access and navigation properties -- every read shape.
    - method: GET
      path: /*
    - method: POST
      path: /*
    - method: PATCH
      path: /*
    - method: DELETE
      path: /*

request.description:
Creates ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0, the OData-to-REST demo, from product-catalog-odata/ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0.yaml.

Note it carries NO policies at all. OData v4 is already REST over HTTP with JSON payloads, so nothing needs transcoding -- the contrast with the SOAP API above is the point of the pair. Each HTTP method is declared once against the catch-all path /*, because OData URLs are open-ended (/Products(3)/Supplier) and cannot be enumerated.

Requires mock-odata-backend.js on port 7194.

Fails with 409 if it already exists -- use 4e instead.

request.description: Idempotent re-push of ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0. Safe to run any time, unlike 4d which returns 409 once the API exists.

Removes ProductCatalogAPI-v1.0 from the gateway. After this the context /product-catalog/v1.0 returns 404.

No request body. Returns 404 if the API is not currently deployed.
